full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J : This rule on an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure against impugned judgment and Order dated 17-2-2011 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Narayangonj in Criminal Revision No. 121 of 2010 disallowing the revision by affirming the Order dated 21-11-2010 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Narayangonj in Narayangonj Model PS Case No. 34 dated 28-10-2011 disallowing the revision. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that one SI of police of Narayangonj Sadar Model PS Narayangonj on 28-10-2010 at about 20-10 hours lodged this FIR with the Narayangonj Sadar PS alleging, inter alia, that on the basis of GD No. 1457 dated 28-10-2010. While the informant and others were no duty, in the meantime, at about 8-00 hours on the basis of secret information, they came to know that having done hoarding and black marketing the petitioner was passing a truck loaded with rice hold goods of OMS to the place of occurrence and having informed the news, the officer-in-charge went at the place of occurrence and could see a truck while it was loaded with the rice hold goods and after making a query to the accused petitioner No.1, he confessed that he purchased OMS rice in Order to sell these rice at Feni. Thereafter, the police have seized the aforesaid truck where there was 17 metric tons rice. Then the petitioner No.1 with the aforesaid truck were taken to the concerned police station and was registered as Narayangonj Sadar Model PS case No. 34 dated 28-10-2010 under section 25(1) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 was started against the accused petitioners. 

 4. Thereafter, the petitioner No.1 was enlarged on bail by this Court in connection with Criminal Miscellaneous case No. 33486 of 2010 and after having heard both the sides the rule was made absolute. 

 5. Mr Sharif U Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the proceeding adopted and constituted against the accused-petitioner are bad in law, without jurisdiction, improper and, as such, the same is liable to be quashed. He further submits that the seized materials are valid in the eye of law and nothing was happened about the hoarding and black marketing intentionally and with the illegal gratification by the others and being manipulated, false case has been lodged against the petitioner. He also submits that the accused was arrested from the inside of our country and the goods were not hoarding in this connection. He cited the case of Gopa Chandra Chowdhury vs State reported in 47 DLR 224 where in stated that when the accused is not apprehended while smuggling goods and he is not arrested with the smuggled goods in border area he cannot be held liable for smuggling punishable under section 25B(1) of the Special Powers Act, 1974. 

 8. It appears from the submission of the learned Advocate for the accused persons that the seized rice has been kept in the open place; that the accused petitioner purchased the rice by giving market price of the same. It further appears from the submission that the seized rice will be damaged if it is remained in open place for some days during this rainy season and in such case the accused-petitioner will suffer irreparable loss and injury. There is substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner. Since the seized rice is perishable item which be damaged if it is kept in the open place during this rainy season and there is no chance of early disposal of the case. So justice will be met if the seized rice can be given in the custody of the accused-petitioner on furnishing reasonable bank guarantee to the satisfaction of the Court concerned.
